title: DCDiff: Enhancing JPEG Compression via Diffusion-based DC Coefficients Estimation
problem: Low-cost cameras cannot support learning-based compressors; one approach drops DC coefficients at camera and reconstructs them later, but statistical reconstruction methods cause deviation-introduced errors that propagate throughout the image.
motivation: JPEG is dominant on low-cost hardware but lacks algorithmic improvements compatible with resource-constrained processors; DC coefficient reconstruction is a bottleneck.
method: DCDiff uses a generative diffusion model to estimate DC coefficients end-to-end rather than relying on statistical methods. It generates masks to correct image locations violating statistical distributions, suppressing error propagation. The approach maintains full JPEG compatibility with typical low-cost processors.
key_novelty: End-to-end generative diffusion model for DC coefficient reconstruction replaces statistical methods, avoiding error propagation and enabling learned priors for natural images.
contributions: End-to-end diffusion-based DC coefficient estimation replacing statistical reconstruction
Mask generation mechanism to correct locations violating statistical distributions
Error propagation suppression through learned priors
Improved compression performance over baselines with minimal impact on downstream tasks; compatible with 2 typical low-cost JPEG processors

metrics.other: Outperforms baselines in compression performance; minimal downstream task impact (specific numbers not provided)

limitations: Abstract does not discuss computational cost of diffusion inference on resource-constrained devices, inference latency, or generalization to different image types.
primary_theme: Diffusion model for JPEG DC coefficient reconstruction
